problems.form_value: human_raters (codebook Section 6: 'Lay raters or crowd workers'); measure_detail says 'Rater expertise is not stated (coded human_raters)'
problems.source_says: The paper says only that two independent raters, blind to condition, scored every idea with one rubric after a prior discussion of the rubric rules and the duplicate deductions. It never says who the raters were or what background they had, so the text supports neither human_raters nor expert_raters. Reconciled forms code this case both ways: c012 S1-O1 keeps human_raters for raters of unstated background, while c056 codes two 'external evaluators' of unstated background as expert_raters because 'nothing suggests lay raters or crowd workers, which is what human_raters covers'. The c075 raters also applied an analytic rubric after calibration, and nothing in the text suggests lay raters. Fix: keep the open question and let Review 1 set one rule for unstated rater background, or ask the authors. Minor: question, construct, unit, AI availability, and every number are unaffected, and codebook Section 8 rule 2 ranks both codes as 'rated by people'.
problems.quote: 평가는 2명의 독립 평가자가 수행하였으며, 평가자는 참여자의 조건 정보를 알 수 없도록 한 상태에서 동일한 루브릭에 따라 채점하였다.
problems.locator: PDF p. 6 (journal p. 45), Section 3.2.4; PDF p. 9 (journal p. 48), Section 5.2, second limitation; codebook Section 6 (Measure); forms c012 S1-O1 and c056 S1-O1 (reconciliation)

confirmed: Criterion 3 holds for S1-O1 to S1-O3. Two independent raters, blind to condition, scored every idea on four dimensions (novelty, usefulness/feasibility, elaboration/specificity, future-change fit). A participant's round score is the sum of up to 10 idea scores (0-100), averaged over the two raters. No outcome is a self-report (PDF p. 5, Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2; PDF p. 6, Sections 3.2.3-3.2.4).

AI availability holds. In round 1, group A could use generative AI and group B worked without it. In round 2, each round-1 group was split at random: A1 kept AI, A2 stopped, B1 adopted AI, B2 stayed without it. So S1-O1 and S1-O2 are yes, and S1-O3 (A2 and B2 in round 2) is no (PDF pp. 4-5, Section 3.1, steps 1 and 3; Figure 1, PDF p. 4).

Question codes follow the codebook rule. S1-O1 and S1-O2 are produced with AI in the treatment arm and are not diversity, so with_ai. In the A1 vs A2 contrast both arms had AI in round 1 and differ only in round-2 AI, so it measures AI assistance, not unassisted work after AI use. S1-O3 compares round-2 output made after AI was removed (A2) with never-AI output (B2), so after_ai (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, step 3; PDF p. 6, Section 3.3.4; PDF p. 8, Section 4.4.2, item 2).

Construct overall_creativity fits. The paper measures creativity as the rubric total ('Creativity was assessed using the total score of a four-dimensional rubric'). No outcome compares outputs across people. The within-round duplicate deduction is a within-person novelty penalty inside the total, not a separate outcome (PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 3.2.2-3.2.3).

Unit participant holds. The paper says the unit of analysis is the individual ('분석 단위는 개인이며'). The t-tests use participant totals, and the mixed model has two scores per person with a random intercept per person (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1; PDF p. 6, Section 3.3.4).

S1-O1 numbers match exactly: adoption effect 28.63 (SE 2.49, z 11.48, p < .001, 95% CI [23.74, 33.52]); discontinuation effect 5.50 (SE 2.47, z 2.23, p = .026, 95% CI [0.67, 10.33]); A1 time effect 8.00 (SE 1.71, z 4.68, 95% CI [4.65, 11.35]); the A1, A2, B1, and B2 rows of Tables 3 and 4; both rows of Table 1. Recomputed gains, paired t, dz, and contrasts (37.73 - 9.10 = 28.63; 8.00 - 2.50 = 5.50) agree (PDF p. 6, Table 1; PDF p. 7, Tables 3-4 and Section 4.4.2; PDF p. 8, Section 4.4.2, item 2).

S1-O2 numbers match exactly: A 63.07 (SD 15.27, n 83), B 29.65 (SD 16.88, n 81), Welch t(159.54) = 13.29, p < .001, difference 33.42, 95% CI [28.45, 38.38], d = 2.08, and no SE is printed. A pooled-SD d and a Welch t recomputed from these give 2.08 and 13.29 (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2).

S1-O3 numbers match Table 4: round 2, A2 64.65 (15.08) vs B2 38.03 (15.18); round 1, 62.15 (14.79) vs 28.93 (18.04); gain 2.50 (4.21) vs 9.10 (8.45). The paper never tests A2 vs B2 (PDF p. 7, Table 4 and Section 4.4.1).
S1-O1 paper_primary holds: the paper reports the time x group_2 planned contrasts as its core results and calls the mixed model its main analysis (PDF p. 6, Section 3.3.4; PDF p. 7, Section 4.3).
Timing immediate holds for all three outcomes: round 2 came after a break of about 30 minutes with a YouTube video, in the same session (PDF p. 2, Introduction; PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, step 2).

The form's caveats hold. The paper calls only the round-2 split random, never says how students entered A or B, and runs no balance test between A and B (PDF p. 2, Introduction; PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, step 3; PDF p. 6, Section 4.1 and Table 1; PDF p. 8, Section 5.1).

No outcome is missing. The paper reports no dimension scores by arm (only rater ICCs), no idea counts by arm (only the pooled means 9.18 and 9.52), and no similarity across people. H2 has no AI contrast and H5 is the difference of the two coded contrasts, and the form's notes list both (PDF p. 5, Section 3.2.2; PDF p. 6, Section 3.2.4; PDF p. 7, Table 2 and Section 4.3; PDF p. 8, Section 4.4.2, item 3).
summary: All three outcomes are rubric scores that two blind raters gave to the ideas the students wrote, and the question, construct, unit, AI availability, and every reported number match the PDF, so criterion 3 holds. The one unsupported field is measure human_raters (lay raters or crowd workers) on all three outcomes: the paper never says who the two raters were, and reconciled forms code this case both ways (c012 human_raters, c056 expert_raters).
